quizzes.title: VB-G RAM G: Objectives and Planning
quizzes.passage:
The Union Government has released Draft Rules under the VB-G RAM G Act. VB-G RAM G is described as a Rural Employment and Livelihood Programme, and the Draft Rules explain how it will operate in practice, including how central funds are allocated and how costs are shared between the Centre and the States.

The Draft Rules move away from an open-ended, demand-driven financing model. Under the new approach, central allocations are determined through a Normative Allocation Formula based on devolution criteria recommended by a Finance Commission. The stated aim is predictability in resource allocation and alignment with the principles of fiscal federalism.

Poorer States are to receive a larger share of funds under the formula. Population is also taken into account because it reflects employment demand, and other socio-economic and governance indicators contribute as well.

Cost sharing is revised to encourage fiscal responsibility. Any expenditure beyond the approved normative allocation must be financed fully by the concerned State Government. The Draft Rules also set out the cost sharing for General States and for Northeastern and Himalayan States. A part of central assistance is linked to performance, judged on parameters such as timely wage payments and compliance with social audit requirements.

Planning under the programme is decentralised and technology-based.

questions.q: What does the acronym VB-G RAM G stand for?
options: Viksit Bharat — Gramin Rozgar Ajeevika Mission — Guarantee
Viksit Bharat — Guarantee for Rural Assets and Modernisation — Gramin
Viksit Bharat — Gramin Rural Ajeevika Mission — Guarantee
Viksit Bharat — Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
questions.explanation: VB-G RAM G stands for Viksit Bharat — Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).

questions.q: Which programme under VB-G RAM G links employment generation with the creation of rural infrastructure?
options: Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack Programme
questions.explanation: The Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack Programme links employment generation with infrastructure creation.

questions.q: Which plan is made mandatory under the Act's decentralised planning?
questions.explanation: The Act makes preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans mandatory.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and the reason.
Assertion (A): VB-G RAM G combines wage employment with the creation of durable rural assets.
Reason (R): The Act's objectives include local planning outcomes.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the listed objective does not explain the wage-plus-assets design.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about VB-G RAM G:
I. The Act is set to replace MGNREGA from July 2026.
II. Preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans is mandatory.
III. The Act does not include rural infrastructure among its objectives.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is false because rural infrastructure is one of the stated objectives, while I and II are true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about VB-G RAM G:
I. Livelihood-supporting facilities are among the assets the infrastructure linkage covers.
II. Climate resilience is among the stated objectives of the Act.
III. The Act is set to replace the National Food Security Act.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the Act replaces MGNREGA, not the National Food Security Act.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT stated as an objective of VB-G RAM G?
questions.explanation: Urban metro expansion is not among the stated objectives, which cover employment, infrastructure, climate resilience and planning.

quizzes.title: VB-G RAM G: Objectives and Planning
quizzes.passage:
The Union Government has released Draft Rules under the VB-G RAM G Act. The Act is described as a Rural Employment and Livelihood Programme and is set to replace MGNREGA. The Draft Rules explain how the programme will operate in practice, including how central funds are allocated and how costs are shared between the Centre and the States.

The planning approach under the programme is decentralised and technology-based. Central allocations are determined through a Normative Allocation Formula based on devolution criteria recommended by a Finance Commission. The stated aim of this shift is predictability in resource allocation and alignment with the principles of fiscal federalism.

Poorer States are to receive a larger share of funds under the formula. Population is taken into account because it reflects employment demand, and other socio-economic and governance indicators also contribute.

Funding is partly linked to performance from the second year onward. The parameters include timely wage payments, compliance with social audit requirements, completion rate of public works and overall implementation efficiency. The Draft Rules state that this is meant to improve accountability and reward efficient States.

questions.q: From which month and year is the Act set to replace MGNREGA?
questions.explanation: The Act is set to replace MGNREGA from July 2026.

questions.q: Which national programme is the Act's technology integration linked with?
questions.explanation: The Act integrates technology planning with PM Gati Shakti.

questions.q: Which plan does the Act make mandatory for decentralised planning?
questions.explanation: The Act makes preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans mandatory.

questions.q: In which year was the VB-G RAM G Act enacted? (Give four digits.)
questions.explanation: The Act is the VB-G RAM G Act 2025.

questions.q: What does the Act combine wage employment with? (Two words.)
questions.explanation: The Act combines wage employment with the creation of durable rural assets.

questions.q: Which type of asset does the infrastructure linkage cover for water? (Two words.)
questions.explanation: The infrastructure linkage covers water conservation assets.

questions.q: Which objective concerns preparing for climate change? (Two words.)
questions.explanation: Climate resilience is one of the Act's stated objectives.

quizzes.title: VB-G RAM G: Governance and Transition
quizzes.passage:
The Union Government has released Draft Rules under the VB-G RAM G Act. The programme is a Rural Employment and Livelihood Programme, and the Act is set to replace MGNREGA from July 2026. The Draft Rules therefore also address the move from the older scheme to the new framework.

The Draft Rules move away from an open-ended, demand-driven financing model towards a Normative Allocation Model. Central allocations are based on devolution criteria recommended by a Finance Commission, which is intended to make resource allocation predictable.

Performance is part of the funding design. A portion of central assistance depends on State performance from the second year onward, judged on timely wage payments, compliance with social audit requirements, completion rate of public works and overall implementation efficiency.

Cost sharing is also revised, with separate shares for General States and for Northeastern and Himalayan States. Any expenditure beyond the approved normative allocation must be financed fully by the concerned State Government.

The Act also provides for national-level bodies to oversee the programme, and the Draft Rules set out how MGNREGA job cards are handled in the transition.

questions.q: How many members does the National Level Steering Committee have?
questions.explanation: The National Level Steering Committee is a 16-member body.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a listed category of members of the National Level Steering Committee?
questions.explanation: Its members come from State Governments, NITI Aayog and relevant Union Ministries, not from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and the reason.
Assertion (A): Workers are to receive Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards under the new framework.
Reason (R): Officials from NITI Aayog are members of the National Level Steering Committee.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but neither explains the other.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Level Steering Committee   ->   A. Remain valid during the transition period
II. Central Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Council   ->   B. Recommends State-wise allocations
III. e-KYC verified MGNREGA Job Cards   ->   C. Advises the Centre on policy implementation
IV. Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards   ->   D. Issued to workers subsequently
Select the correct answer.
questions.explanation: The Steering Committee recommends allocations, the Council advises on policy, e-KYC job cards remain valid, and cards are issued subsequently.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the national-level bodies under VB-G RAM G:
I. The Steering Committee monitors implementation and compliance.
II. The Council reviews programme performance.
III. e-KYC verified MGNREGA Job Cards are cancelled at the start of the transition period.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is false because e-KYC verified job cards remain valid during the transition period.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the national-level bodies under VB-G RAM G:
I. The Council is chaired by the Union Rural Development Secretary.
II. The Steering Committee includes officials from NITI Aayog.
III. The Council advises the Centre on policy implementation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the Council is chaired by the Union Minister for Rural Development.

questions.q: Which minister chairs the Central Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Council?
questions.explanation: The Council is chaired by the Union Minister for Rural Development.

The Draft Rules move away from an open-ended, demand-driven financing model towards a Normative Allocation Model. Central allocations are based on devolution criteria recommended by a Finance Commission, which is meant to make resource allocation predictable.

Performance is part of the funding design. A portion of central assistance depends on State performance from the second year, judged on timely wage payments, compliance with social audit requirements, completion rate of public works and overall implementation efficiency.

Cost sharing is also revised, with separate shares for General States and for Northeastern and Himalayan States. Any expenditure beyond the approved normative allocation must be financed fully by the concerned State Government.

The Act also provides for national-level oversight of the programme. The Draft Rules set out how MGNREGA job cards are handled during the transition period.

questions.q: How many members does the National Level Steering Committee have?
questions.explanation: The Committee is a 16-member body.

questions.q: Which minister chairs the Central Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Council? (Give the designation.)
questions.explanation: The Council is chaired by the Union Minister for Rural Development.

questions.q: What type of verification must MGNREGA job cards have to remain valid during the transition period?
questions.explanation: e-KYC verified MGNREGA job cards remain valid during the transition period.

questions.q: What card will workers subsequently receive under the new framework? (Give the full name.)
questions.explanation: Workers subsequently receive Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards under the new framework.

questions.q: Officials from which body are members of the National Level Steering Committee?
questions.explanation: The Committee includes officials from NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Which body advises the Centre on policy implementation? (Give the full name.)
questions.explanation: The Central Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Council advises the Centre on policy implementation.

questions.q: Which committee recommends State-wise allocations?
questions.explanation: The National Level Steering Committee recommends State-wise allocations.
